extracted.intended_audience: public relations and corporate communications professionals (crisis communicators, PR managers)
extracted.subtask_short: crisis PR response for viral video
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and executing a corporate crisis response when an employee-posted viral video threatens brand reputation, using legal, operational, and social-media tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying and taking action against the culprits
rubrics_metrics.description: The company started by capturing digital images of the two employees' faces from the video and distributed a message to all US locations seeking help in identifying them by name. Upon confirming their identities and pinpointing the location, it then contacted the storeowner and requested that they be fired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect digital stills from the video; solicit identification via internal channels; confirm identities and location; contact the franchisee/storeowner to terminate employment; because authenticity may be uncertain, involve authorities—Domino's contacted the Health Department and local police to file charges. Be prepared to act quickly but verify facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting the video removed
rubrics_metrics.description: The company's social media team immediately contacted YouTube to ask that the video be removed since it was in violation of several of the site's guidelines. YouTube responded that it would pull the video only at the copyright owner's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the copyright owner (e.g., the person who filmed it). Obtain a signed authorization from the copyright owner (legal counsel involvement advisable) and present it to the hosting platform. Be prepared to meet in person and produce legal documents if needed. Understand platform policies and that platforms may defer to copyright claims over policy complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to public queries (avoid immediate broad press release)
rubrics_metrics.description: Domino's decided it best not to go public with a press release or news conference right away. Instead, it responded to those who approached the company about the story and communicated with forums that had posted or hosted conversations about the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid issuing a wide public statement immediately (which can drive curiosity and spread). Prioritize direct responses to inbound queries and to the specific forums where the content is being discussed; drive home that the incident was perpetrated against the company. When appropriate, post a clear statement on the corporate website and enter the conversation on social platforms to direct people to the official message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fighting fire with fire (post a company video response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three days after the original incident, Domino's posted its own video to YouTube featuring company president Patrick Doyle addressing the issue, calmly and sincerely, venting his anger and reiterating how sacred the company holds its customers' trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authentic, unscripted video from leadership to address the issue directly and sincerely. Use platform-native content (e.g., YouTube) and amplify via the company's social accounts (Twitter, Facebook). Craft titles and metadata strategically (see SEO tactic below) so the company video surfaces in searches. A frank leadership presence can change the narrative from 'what happened' to 'what the company is doing about it.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Line up your ducks ahead of time (preparedness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although every crisis is unique and no protocol will fit every occasion, it pays to follow the Boy Scout mantra and always be prepared. It was fortunate for Domino's that it already had a social media team in place to respond as needed, and well-trained staff throughout the company able to quickly take up the tasks at hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and train a social media/crisis team in advance; have clear operational processes (supplier chains, recall mechanisms) and empowered managers who can act without boardroom delays. Senior management must consent to trust frontline responders. Cultivate strong customer loyalty ahead of time—existing goodwill aids reputation recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do what you can to curb the propagation
rubrics_metrics.description: By initially responding only within the forums where the story was already unleashed, Domino's was able to keep the issue somewhat manageable until it had a better understanding of what had happened and could begin taking steps to rectify the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit broad amplification until you understand the facts. Avoid media appearances that would require replaying or linking to the offending content (e.g., talk-show segments showing the original video). Ask media partners to avoid airing the offensive content when possible; prioritize containment tactics while preparing corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest and state your case
rubrics_metrics.description: Never try to hide that the incident occurred. Although Domino's sought to limit the conversation, the company did respond to every incoming query—openly and truthfully, with criticism against the perpetrators and contending that it had been victimized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond transparently: acknowledge the incident, condemn the perpetrators, explain actions being taken (discipline, legal action, remediation). Openness prevents being painted as evasive and helps reframe the story. Use truthful, off-the-cuff responses when appropriate, but ensure factual accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue with 'business as usual'
rubrics_metrics.description: Some felt suspending all advertising and lying low would be best. Domino's disagreed and continued running existing ads (with no 'we're sorry' messaging); the involved store was sanitized and quickly reopened for business, and planned product launches proceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For retail/consumer brands, maintaining normal marketing and product activity preserves top-of-mind awareness and aids recovery. Sanitize and remediate the specific operational locus of the incident quickly, then resume normal operations and campaigns rather than centering marketing on apologies unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use search/SEO tactics and social channels to influence results
rubrics_metrics.description: In posting the company response, Domino's used the word 'disgusting' in the video title—just as had been done with the original video—so that the new video would come up first when users searched for the original. The company then posted links to its video on Twitter and on its Facebook page wall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionally choose titles, keywords, and copy that match the search terms people use for the negative content so your corrective content ranks higher. Amplify that content through corporate social accounts to drive views and change search/result prominence. Monitor metrics (views, search queries, media impressions) to assess reach and narrative change.
